name: Nuwara Eliya tea
region: Nuwara Eliya agro-climatic region, Central Province
flavor_summary: Sri Lanka Tea Board regulations, section 1(d), describe the regional brewed tea as fragrant and delicate. Section 2 and the annexes define the product by its listed regional gardens and factories.
scope_note: Black-tea interpretation corroborated by the producer's Nuwara Eliya BOP regional collection; tasting words remain from the Tea Board regional specification. Central Province is a geographic display grouping, not the certification extent.

name: Shan Tuyet green tea
region: Hoàng Su Phì, source-era Hà Giang Province, northern Vietnam
flavor_summary: The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism page identifies green tea and Shan Tuyet in Hoang Su Phi and names producing communes. It does not establish a specific tasting note for this green product; no sensory word is assigned.
scope_note: GeoNames Hoang Su Phi is used only as a named regional reference. Display uses the archived Ha Giang province outline from the source period, not present-day administrative claims or the full Shan Tuyet GI.

name: Thai iced tea
flavor_summary: MICHELIN Guide's Bangkok barista interviews describe cha yen, sweetened condensed milk and ice; the article also lists Bangkok venues. The label summarizes the drink's ingredients and service, not a cultivar tasting note.
scope_note: Cup near Bangkok is an example drinking location, not the drink's birthplace, an exclusive distribution or a tea-growing region. Recipes vary; no spice or artificial color is asserted for every cup.

name: Masala chiya
flavor_summary: GIZ NepalTrade issue 3 (May 2012), PDF page 12, describes Nepali-style masala chiya made by simmering milk, water, CTC tea, sugar and spices, then straining; it states that recipes vary. ECS Nepal's on-location account documents chiya shops in Kathmandu, not a unique city recipe.
scope_note: Cup near Kathmandu is an example urban drinking location, not a growing region or a birthplace claim. The English label uses the publication's spelling masala chiya; native name is a transliteration, not a quoted official registration.
